key_insight: An automated AI pipeline can extract labels from CMR reports and, using multimodal vision models, accurately identify several cardiomyopathies and normal scans from conventional CMR images.
clinical_relevance: This could support faster, more standardized CMR interpretation and help scale diagnostic assistance in settings with limited expert readers.
method: Used locally run open-source LLMs to pull diagnostic labels from narrative CMR reports and curate multimodal CMR data.
Fine-tuned three vision foundation models (DINO, VST, UMedPT) on cine and late-gadolinium-enhancement (LGE) sequences in a two-stage workflow.
Combined model and modality outputs with ensemble strategies to improve diagnostic robustness.
evidence_signal: The study trained on 988 curated cases, validated on 246, and reported performance on an independent test set of 1,067 patients, with top AUCs reaching 0.966 for cardiac amyloidosis and 0.959 for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
watch_item: Performance was strong, but real-world use still needs external validation, workflow integration, and confirmation that automated label extraction remains reliable across sites and report styles.
paper_title: Development of an automated, reliable, and clinically meaningful artificial intelligence (AI) tool for diagnosing cardiac disease from conventional cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) images
